To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the interacting domains of two proteins that are required for the formation and function of BLOC-1.
the HPS1 N- and C-terminal regions are required for the formation and stability of the BLOC-3 complex, and missense mutations found to cause HPS-1 do not affect interaction of HPS1 with HPS4.
the HPS1-HPS4 interaction is required for BLOC-3 formation and that missense mutations found to cause HPS-1 do not disrupt this interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular basis of a rare disease called Hermansky-Puddlak syndrome.
the biogenesis of the lysosome-related organnelle complex-3 and the identification of the molecular defects responsible for the Hermansky-Puclk syndrome.
the identification of the regions in HPS proteins required for the formation and function of the BLOC-3 complex and the characterization of HPS mutations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction between HPS-1 and HPS-4 is required for BLOC-3 formation, which is essential in the formation of lysosome related organelles.
HPS-1 mutations that cause instability of the HPS-1 protein are more severe than those that cause a loss-of-function of BLOC- 3.

the HPS1 N- and C-terminal regions and the HPS4 middle region are required for BLOC-3 formation and that the N- and middle portions of the HPS4 protein bind to the N- and the middle portions of the human HPS1 protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPS1 and 4 interact with each others and the interaction between these two proteins is important for BLOC-3 formation.
the N- and middle regions of HPS1 are required for the interaction with HPS1, and the N- and mid-regions of HPS1 interact with HPS4.

the N-terminal portion of HPS-1 (residutes 1-249) interacts with a region in the middle of the HPS-4 protein (residues ~300-500) while the C-terminus of HPS-4 (residutes ~400-500) interacts with both N- and C-terminal regions of HPS- 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the interacting regions in the HPS4 protein that interact with the HPS1 N-terminal domain.
the HPS-1 protein contains a C-terminal region that is not required for interaction with HPS-4.
the HPS1/HPS4 interaction is important for BLOC-3 stability and that mutations that affect this interaction may be more severe in terms of the disease phenotype.
